thread:
alex: Hey team, running into an import error after pip installing the python SDK inside a Debian slim container. Happens on import redwood. Anyone seen protobuf-related failures recently?

jen_support: Ugh, seen a few of those. Can you paste the traceback and pip list?

alex: Here's the trace when running `python -c "import redwood;"` inside the image: 
```
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "<stdin>", line 1, in <module>
  File "/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/redwood/__init__.py", line 12, in <module>
    from google.protobuf import descriptor_pool
ImportError: cannot import name 'descriptor_pool' from 'google.protobuf' (/usr/local/lib/python3.11/site-packages/google/protobuf/__init__.py)
```

alex: pip freeze: 
```
redwood==0.9.2
protobuf==4.23.4
grpcio==1.56.0
requests==2.31.0
```

maya_dev: That looks like the common protobuf C-extension vs pure-Python compatibility issue. protobuf v4 removed some import paths and changed internals. Our last SDK pin was compatible with protobuf <4 but it slipped through in a system that had protobuf 4.x installed.

sam_sre: What base image? Debian slim sometimes pulls system protobuf from apt during other layers. Also check if there's a global site-packages in the build step.

alex: Dockerfile: 
```
FROM python:3.11-slim
WORKDIR /app
COPY pyproject.toml .
RUN pip install -U pip setuptools poetry
RUN pip install .[all]
```

alex: Also ran `python -c "import google.protobuf; print(google.protobuf.__version__)"` -> `4.23.4`

jen_support: Quick workaround: pin protobuf to 3.20.x for now. `pip install "protobuf<4,>=3.19.0"` and rebuild image. That usually restores the missing symbols.

maya_dev: Agreed. Longer term we should update the SDK to be protobuf-4 compatible or vendor the parts we need. I'll open an internal task. For immediate repro: can you reproduce in a clean venv?

alex: Reproduced in fresh venv on macOS too. Steps: 
1) python -m venv venv 
2) . venv/bin/activate 
3) pip install redwood==0.9.2 
4) python -c "import redwood" -> same ImportError.

sam_sre: Can you try `pip install protobuf==3.20.3` then import?

alex: After pinning: 
```
$ pip install protobuf==3.20.3
Collecting protobuf==3.20.3
Installing collected packages: protobuf
Successfully installed protobuf-3.20.3
$ python -c "import redwood; print('import ok')"
import ok
```

jen_support: Great — that confirms the mismatch. Saving workaround in the support KB: recommend pinning protobuf <4 until SDK rev is released.

maya_dev: Filed task RDW-1284 to add explicit runtime dependency `protobuf<4` and to test compatibility with 4.x. Also adding unit test that tries import with latest protobuf to detect regressions.

pkg-bot: Note: workaround affects customers who rely on system-installed protobuf (apt). Recommend calling out container rebuild guidance in KB.

alex: One more oddity: we saw it break only when installing the extras `.[all]` — could that pull a different protobuf?

maya_dev: extras can bring optional deps (grpcio-tools, etc.). grpcio-tools sometimes drags a different protobuf wheel. Use `pip check` to see incompatibilities.

alex: `pip check` output: 
```
No broken requirements found.
```

jen_support: Even if `pip check` is clean, import-time symbol errors can still happen due to incompatible major versions. KB entry will include commands to diagnose: 
```
python -c "import google; import google.protobuf; print(google.__file__, google.protobuf.__file__, google.protobuf.__version__)"
pip show redwood protobuf grpcio
```

sam_sre: Also adding a note to image build docs: run `pip install --no-cache-dir --use-feature=2020-resolver redwood.[all] protobuf<4` to ensure resolver pins compatible set.

alex: Thanks all — workaround worked and blocked my release. Please link KB and the task.

maya_dev: KB: https://redwood-internal/kb/python-sdk-protobuf-incompat (drafted). Assigned RDW-1284.

jen_support: I'll follow up with the customer-facing support article after dev confirms timeline. :white_check_mark:

alex: Closing this thread for now, will reopen if any other import errors crop up. :thumbsup:
